referents.why: 'to them' is the people, the crowd. The crowd is first named in Mrk.15.8, not in an earlier verse or in this one, so no candidate fits.
'whom' is the relative pronoun of the prisoner: masculine singular, matching the one prisoner (w6) in this verse.
'he used to release' has Pilate as subject, the one the custom belongs to. Pilate is named in Mrk.15.5.
'they requested' is the same people as 'to them': the crowd, which is not a candidate here.

links.why: Self-link: a clause is not the next event after itself.
The relative clause 'whom they requested' is nested in the noun phrase 'one prisoner' inside cl0.

none_fit.what: A background aside about Pilate's custom before the next event. The only cross-verse link is and, which does not mark background.

cant_tell.what: Who the people are in this verse.
cant_tell.why: The Greek gives only pronouns for them. The crowd is named only in Mrk.15.8, so both pronouns are left as none.
